An $n$-component GMM is defined as [S1, unofficial]:

The claim states that an n-component GMM is defined as $p(x|Θ) = ∑_{i}^{n} ω_i N (x; μ_i , Σ_i )$, where $N (x; μ, Σ)$ is a parametric d-dimensional Gaussian distribution with mean $μ ∈ ℝ^d$, covariance $Σ ∈ ℝ^{d×d}$, and $x$ is a d-dimensional vector. Source [S1] explicitly provides this exact definition in the Appendix section: 'Given a parametric d-dimensional Gaussian distribution N (x; µ, Σ) with mean µ ∈ Rd , covariance Σ ∈ Rd×d and d-dimensional vector x, an n-component GMM is given as p(x|Θ) = ∑ ωi N (x; µi , Σi ).' All components of the claim are present and consistent with the evidence.
